analysis.title: GS Joseph - Macro Reads 22 Nov 2026
key_insights: USD acted as safe haven in a policy-driven risk-off week, with strength rotating from DM to EM. GS 2027 FX Outlook still sees a gradual USD softening, but investors must 'time the turn' as markets only see the peak of hiking cycles in hindsight.
USD/JPY is back near 160 on hawkish Fed repricing. Japan FX chief Mimura called moves 'excessively rapid', and GS thinks MoF intervention likelihood rises above 160. GS favors short EUR/JPY.

EM FX came under severe pressure from USD strength, local disappointments and lower positioning. GS favors COP longs (constructive fiscal, high carry) and ZAR (another SARB hike expected) and ILS shorts.

INR is the best performing EM/G10 currency over the week and month vs USD, breaking below 93 for first time since April. Drivers are low AI leverage, five straight weeks of foreign equity inflows and RBI rebuilding carry. GS is sceptical spot gains extend at this pace. Long INR/short IDR stops tightened.

AUD/NZD fell on a hawkish RBNZ (GS now sees 25bp hikes in Dec and March), weak Australian labor data (third straight upside unemployment surprise), and lower energy and copper. GS expects AUD/NZD to unwind its gains.

Rates: risk-off has undone much of the hawkish front-end repricing. GS favors 5y outperformance in the US via 3m5y vs 3m2y receivers, Bund longs, UK curve longs, and 2s10s JGB flatteners (entry 94bp, target 75bp, stop 105bp).

US equity flows: HFs net sold US equities a 3rd straight week, with ETF shorting up 11%, the largest since March. Single stocks were shorted every day, the largest weekly shorting since Jun '22. 9 of 11 sectors net sold.

US equity vol is in extreme stress. SPX fell 7 straight sessions, VIX is above 35, term structure is inverted, skew is steep. GS vol panic index is 9.8/10, and readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief.

High-Beta Cyclicals are +12% YTD while US AI basket is negative YTD. GS flags 4Q 2018 as an analog, when High Beta Cyclicals fell 23% and underperformed SPX by 10pp if growth worries take over from inflation worries.

Asia: MXAPJ fell 8.3% as AI unwind intensified, with Taiwan -17% and Korea -9%. EM Asia ex-China had US$7.4bn FII outflows. Taiwan margin MMR near margin-call threshold raises forced-deleveraging risk.
GS cut Taiwan to Marketweight and the end-2027 TAIEX target to 50,000 (about 40% upside, 40% implied vol). It also cut China A to Marketweight, and raised China H and India to Overweight.
China 2027 targets are MSCI China 85 (+33%) and CSI300 4500 (+14%). India NIFTY target is 28,500 by end-2027, with 15% EPS growth in CY27 and CY28 and foreign ownership at a decade-plus low.

GS Economics 2027 Outlook: GDP growth 2.4%, core PCE falling to 2.4% by late 2027. Two more 25bp Fed hikes in December and March to 4.25-4.5%, then cuts starting November 2027. Williams pushed back on a 50bp December hike.
GS cross-asset trade ideas from 2027 outlooks include dual binaries on EURUSD/USDJPY/SPX, long EGP/NGN, long KRW/INR/TWD via puts and digitals.
ASEAN data-center bank exposure concerns look overdone. China-linked AI workloads are 0.5-0.75GW, or 15-25% of ASEAN live demand, and bank exposure is no more than about 3% of loans where disclosed.

sector_views.rationale: GS raised India industrials to overweight and remains overweight Banks, Utilities, TMT and Defense.
If 2018-style growth scare develops, this pocket would underperform sharply.
Cut to Marketweight on AI-capex risk, concentration, valuation premium and 40% implied vol despite 32%/25% EPS growth.
